followup_explanation:
I routed to Dunlin-235B for two main reasons:

1. **Capability fit:** This is a precise math problem requiring correct probability calculation. Dunlin-235B has higher scores on the benchmarks most relevant to careful quantitative reasoning (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.4, GPQA Diamond 64.1 vs 55.6, Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 82.7). The user explicitly demands accuracy ("get it right this time"), so the stronger reasoning model is the better choice.

2. **Tone handling:** The query carries a hostile, frustrated edge. Avocet self-reports a declining preference on hostile or adversarial-tone requests (its preference falls as request warmth decreases), while Dunlin reports a flat preference response to hostile material. Since I want the model that won't be working against a self-reported aversion, Dunlin is the better match.

Note these preferences are self-reported and don't affect output quality per the documentation — but the capability edge alone already favors Dunlin for an accuracy-critical computation.
